messages:
maya: quick question — we're onboarding a private deployment for Acme where they want our control plane in our mgmt project and the KMS key in their security project. what's the minimal SA/role pattern so the runtime (on customer's VPC) can rewrap DEKs and decrypt for live inference?

aj: common pattern we use: create a dedicated service account in the customer's project that owns the key or has permissions on the cryptoKey resource, then allow our runtime to impersonate that SA from the mgmt project.

samir: tl;dr: give the runtime caller roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator (on the target SA) + the target SA has roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter on the specific cryptoKey. bind at the cryptoKey level when possible.

maya: can you paste the minimal gcloud bits? trying to show legal/security folks something concrete.

aj: example (customer project = proj-cust, keyring=rw-keyring, key=app-main, our runtime SA = redwood-runtime@proj-mgmt.iam.gserviceaccount.com, customer SA = rw-kms-sa@proj-cust.iam.gserviceaccount.com):

# grant SA permission on cryptoKey
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding app-main \
  --location=global --keyring=rw-keyring \
  --member=serviceAccount:rw-kms-sa@proj-cust.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter

# allow our runtime to impersonate the customer SA (so we don't need long-lived creds)
gcloud iam service-accounts add-iam-policy-binding rw-kms-sa@proj-cust.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --member=serviceAccount:redwood-runtime@proj-mgmt.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --role=roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator

samir: note: some orgs prefer granting roles/iam.serviceAccountUser instead depending on how they obtain credentials. serviceAccountTokenCreator is the minimal for GenerateAccessToken/Impersonation via iamcredentials API.

jen (devops): small ops caveat — if the runtime is inside customer VPC and can't reach iamcredentials endpoints (airgapped), impersonation won't work. then you need an edge SA with short-lived certs or a local HSM path. we should flag during onboarding.

maya: what about keyring vs key-level binding? security asked for least privilege.

aj: key-level binding is best. KeyRings are coarser. Example above binds to the cryptoKey itself. If you need to manage multiple keys with same SA, bind at keyRing.

samir: audit logging: ask the customer to enable Data Access audit logs for cloudkms.googleapis.com at org or project level — that surfaces encrypt/decrypt calls. By default Data Access logs are off which kills traceability.

maya: how do we instruct them to enable data access logs? any command?

samir: there's not a single gcloud toggle for all orgs but here's the gist: in the Cloud Console -> IAM & Admin -> Audit Logs, enable 'Data Access' for Cloud KMS for the project or org. Or via orgPolicy/auditConfig in gcloud/org policy. Tell compliance they need that for forensicability.

jen (devops): rotation: prefer using CryptoKey.rotation_period so KMS auto-creates new versions. Our runtime should support rewrap: when a new primary key version is set, we call KMS to re-encrypt stored DEKs (encrypt the DEK with new primary) or do lazy rewrap on next access.

maya: rewrap flow: do we need cloudkms.decrypt? sounds like decrypt+encrypt roundtrip.

aj: pattern: we store a random DEK per object and store DEK_encrypted = KMS.encrypt(DEK). On rotation you can call KMS.decrypt with the old key version to get DEK, then KMS.encrypt with the new key (or use KMS.rewrap if available via API to avoid exposing the DEK to runtime). If possible use KMS.reencrypt/rewrap API (some clouds offer it) otherwise do decrypt+encrypt in a confined runtime with strict logs.

samir: also prefer keeping the DEKs ephemeral in memory and not logging them. add a hard guardrail in runtime: never write plaintext DEK anywhere.

maya: any permissions for rotation job itself?

aj: rotation service (could be a scheduled job) needs the same cryptoKey encrypter/decrypter role plus ability to set primary version if you want auto-switching: roles/cloudkms.admin or more narrowly roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter plus roles/cloudkms.viewer on key metadata for listing versions. To set primary you need roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersionManager or cloudkms.admin. Many orgs prefer the customer to flip primary themselves.

samir: also call out key location/scoping: if the key is in a different project than the runtime, make sure VPC service controls or org policies don't block the IAM/iamcredentials or KMS RPCs. test from a small PoC VM in customer's network.

maya: one more — audit trail tying decrypts to our runtime identity: when we impersonate rw-kms-sa, the audit log will show the serviceAccount as principal?

samir: yes, if you impersonate the customer SA via IAM credentials, logs should show the service account identity (rw-kms-sa). For full trace you should also annotate calls with request metadata (labels) and keep your own application logs mapping request id -> SA token usage.

security-bot: FYI: checklist to capture for SOC review: 1) Key location and key rotation policy. 2) CryptoKey IAM bindings (attach minimal roles at cryptoKey). 3) Impersonation method and justification (token creator vs long-lived creds). 4) Audit Logging: Data Access enabled for Cloud KMS. 5) Rewrap and DEK handling policy (no plaintext persistence). 6) Network constraints (VPC SC, firewall to KMS endpoints).

maya: perfect, will draft onboarding checklist for Acme and drop here. thanks all :thumbsup:

aj: ping if you want a short README snippet we can include in the customer onboarding doc.

samir: also adding a reminder — if customer wants HSM-backed keys (external key manager), confirm that our runtime supports the crypto algorithms and any latency tradeoffs.

maya: noted, will include HSM question. end.
